description: The Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker from Global Energy Monitor (GEM), a non-profit research organisation, gives asset-level data on gas transmission pipelines and liquefied natural gas (LNG) import and export terminals worldwide, with a companion LNG carrier tracker. On 26 September 2026 the page counted 4,158 pipelines with 1.5 million km of combined length and 1,207 LNG terminal projects. Records give routes or locations, capacity, length, status, owners, start year and capital cost estimates, and each project has a GEM.wiki page. The latest releases were November 2025 for pipelines, September 2025 for LNG terminals and June 2026 for LNG carriers. Coverage is global. Access is through a free online tracker map, dashboards and summary tables, and the full data set is a spreadsheet downloadable through a short download form on GEM's site, under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: only transmission pipelines are covered, not distribution networks, and component release dates differ. Simulation uses are gas network flow and security of supply models, supply disruption scenarios and hazard exposure of pipelines and terminals. Related records: data-gem-global-integrated-power-tracker combines GEM's power trackers and data-gem-global-energy-ownership-tracker maps owners.
